assembly_instructions: 1. Bolt the concrete base slab to the floor and install the two brushed-steel X rails and two carbon-fiber Z rails as the root frame. 2. Mount four vertical steel posts and the upper crossbeam so the architecture reads as a single exposed rack rather than a solid chassis. 3. Install the front input deck at y=0.16 m: text lane in the centre, image lane at X=-4.8 m, and audio lane at X=-6.8 m. 4. Add the image Pan-and-Scan wheel above the image plate, then the SigLIP-2 encoder and its projector; add the audio mel filterbank, USM encoder, and matching projector on the audio lane. 5. Route both modality projectors and the text embedding table into the central embedding slab, then bolt the residual spine through the slab and up the rack. 6. Stack the exposed 7:1 attention group around the spine: seven thin local trays followed by one thicker global tray, then add the compressed continuation marker for layers 9-79 and the final global tray. 7. Attach the exploded representative block bay to the right side of the rack in assembly order: attention pre-norm, QKV projection, QK norm, RoPE gear, attention mask, attention kernel, O projection, FFN pre-norm, SwiGLU, FFN post-norm, and residual merge links. 8. Mount the amber KV-cache column on the left memory rail and connect it only to attention/global trays; mount the cyan latent-summary capsules on the right memory rail and connect them to the global attention path. 9. Install the LM head and loss sphere at the top of the residual spine, then mount the Gemini teacher slab on its own bracket and connect it to the loss node for KL distillation. 10. Add the training corpus tray, AdamW state blocks, and TPU parallelism frame along the rear rail; connect them to the trainable stack but keep them offset so inference dataflow remains visible.

info.english_name: Gemma 4 (projected flagship, ~70B dense, native audio + vision)
info.summary: PROJECTED next-generation flagship from Google DeepMind, extrapolated from Gemma 3's published research direction. No public paper at scene time. Best guess: stays DENSE (DeepMind's Gemma identity) at ~70B params (up from 27B), 80 layers × ~7168 hidden, GQA(48/8), local:global attention pushed from 5:1 to 7:1 with a smaller 512-token local window, dual pre+post RMSNorm and QK-Norm preserved, native multimodal on BOTH image (SigLIP-2 + Pan&Scan) AND audio (USM-style encoder), 1M context via global RoPE base 4M, distilled from a larger Gemini teacher.
info.description:
Gemma 4 is presented here as a research-trajectory PROJECTION, not a paper. Where Gemma 3 went dense at 27B with 5:1 LOCAL:GLOBAL attention and image-only multimodal, Gemma 4 likely (i) jumps to ~70B dense (still no MoE — DeepMind has stayed dense across the Gemma line on purpose, citing serving simplicity), (ii) pushes local:global to 7:1 to make 1M context cheap, with a SMALLER 512-token window (was 1024) compensated by global layers carrying more of the long-range work, (iii) adds native AUDIO input via a USM-style encoder, complementing the existing SigLIP image path, (iv) extends global RoPE base from 1M to 4M for clean 1M-token extrapolation, (v) adds an OPTIONAL latent-compressed summary cache that persists across requests for shared system prompts and long documents, (vi) keeps the dual pre+post RMSNorm and QK-Norm of Gemma 3 — both shipped because they're clean stability wins.

Design rationale, in one line each:
• Stay dense at 70B: avoids the operational cost of expert all-to-all; one model, one inference path.
• 7:1 local-global with 512-token window: KV cache is dominated by the 11–12 global layers; locals are nearly free at 1M ctx.
• Audio + image multimodal: audio is the next obvious modality after vision; consistent with Gemini's multimodal-from-day-one philosophy.
• Latent summary cache: shared system prompts get a tiny persistent representation rather than KV reuse — works across model versions.
• Distillation from Gemini: Gemma's whole story; bigger teacher → bigger Gemma student.

comparisons.delta: Gemma 3 was dense 27B with 5:1 local:global attention, 1024-token local window, image-only multimodal, 128K context, RoPE base 1M for global. Projected Gemma 4 grows to 70B dense, pushes local:global to 7:1 with a HALVED 512-token window, adds audio modality, jumps context 128K → 1M with global RoPE base 4M, and adds a projected new latent-summary cache for prompt sharing across requests. QK-Norm and dual pre+post RMSNorm stay.

Two generations of distance. Gemma 4 keeps the dense + distillation philosophy but replaces every load-bearing block with 7:1 local-global GQA + QK-Norm + dual norm + multimodal vision/audio + 1M context. Vocab 256K stays.

Fundamental philosophical difference: Gemma 4 is DENSE where V4-Pro and GLM-5.1 are sparse MoE. At 70B Gemma 4 activates all 70B per token (vs ~48B for projected GLM-5.1 at 600B total). Gemma's pitch: simpler deployment (no expert all-to-all), smaller absolute footprint, but lower per-parameter capacity ceiling. The 7:1 local-global trick gives Gemma 4 a KV-cache advantage even at 1M context — most layers only need 512-token windows.

Public consensus on GPT-5-class peers is unstable. Gemma 4 stays dense and small relative to closed peers, betting on (i) distillation from a much larger Gemini teacher to close the per-parameter quality gap, (ii) native multimodal audio + image, (iii) the local-global attention plan as the route to cheap 1M context. Where closed peers favour quality at any cost, Gemma 4 favours serving cost.

parts.name: Open Concrete Diagram Base
parts.role: Thin floor datum that roots every subsystem and makes any floating component visually obvious.

parts.name: Front X Rail
parts.role: Front structural rail tying the text, image, and audio input stations into one assembly.

parts.name: Rear X Rail
parts.role: Rear structural rail carrying training, teacher, and parallelism support modules.

parts.name: Left Z Rail
parts.role: Left side rail that fixes the audio input lane and memory-cache column to the frame.

parts.name: Right Z Rail
parts.role: Right side rail that fixes the latent-cache and training support brackets to the frame.

parts.name: Front Left Rack Post
parts.role: Vertical post supporting the exposed transformer rack without hiding the layer interiors.

parts.name: Front Right Rack Post
parts.role: Vertical post supporting the exposed transformer rack and keeping the local/global trays aligned.

parts.name: Back Left Rack Post
parts.role: Rear vertical post bracing the central stack while leaving the rear exploded bay visible.

parts.name: Back Right Rack Post
parts.role: Rear vertical post bracing the central stack and the right-side latent-cache bracket.

parts.name: Upper Front Crossbeam
parts.role: Top rail that shows the layer tower is an open rack rather than an opaque box.

parts.name: Upper Back Crossbeam
parts.role: Rear top rail carrying the teacher and training brackets without covering the transformer trays.

parts.name: Input Tokens Plate
parts.role: Text token intake for the 256K multilingual SentencePiece vocabulary before embedding lookup.

parts.name: Image Input Plate
parts.role: Image intake plate representing variable-resolution pictures before crop slicing.

parts.name: Pan-and-Scan Crop Wheel
parts.role: Crop wheel that splits non-square images into overlapping 896×896 SigLIP tiles.

parts.name: SigLIP-2 Vision Encoder
parts.role: Frozen vision encoder producing projected soft tokens from each image crop.

parts.name: Vision Projector to d=7168
parts.role: Linear adapter that maps SigLIP-2 soft tokens into the LLM residual width.

parts.name: Audio Waveform Plate
parts.role: Projected native audio intake for raw 16 kHz waveform segments.

parts.name: 80-Mel Filterbank
parts.role: Signal-processing shelf that converts waveform frames into 80-mel log-spectrogram features.

parts.name: USM-Style Audio Encoder
parts.role: Projected frozen conformer encoder producing about 30 audio tokens per second.
parts.memory_footprint: Frozen encoder weights projected around 1 GiB BF16.
parts.algorithm:
mel = log_mel(audio, n_mels=80)
tokens_audio = conformer(mel)
h_audio = audio_proj(tokens_audio)

parts.name: Audio Projector to d=7168
parts.role: Linear adapter that maps USM-style audio tokens into the LLM residual width.

parts.name: Embedding and Tied LM Table
parts.role: Shared embedding and output table with about 256000 by 7168 BF16 parameters.

parts.name: Exposed Residual Spine
parts.role: Continuous d=7168 residual stream passing through the 80-layer dense stack.

parts.name: Layer 1 Local Tray
parts.role: First sliding-window transformer tray with 512-token local attention.

parts.name: Layer 2 Local Tray
parts.role: Second local tray showing the repeated 512-token sliding-window pattern.

parts.name: Layer 3 Local Tray
parts.role: Third local tray, still using compact ring-buffer KV storage rather than full-context KV.

parts.name: Layer 4 Local Tray
parts.role: Fourth local tray in the 7:1 group, making the local-dominated cadence visible.

parts.name: Layer 5 Local Tray
parts.role: Fifth local tray, representing cheap near-neighbour attention at one-million-token context.

parts.name: Layer 6 Local Tray
parts.role: Sixth local tray, placed separately so it does not merge into a featureless block.

parts.name: Layer 7 Local Tray
parts.role: Seventh local tray immediately before the full-context global layer in the projected cadence.

parts.name: Layer 8 Global Tray
parts.role: Full-context attention tray using RoPE base 4M and carrying most long-range dependency work.

parts.name: Compressed Layers 9-79 Stack Marker
parts.role: Open marker for the repeated middle of the 80-layer dense stack; it is intentionally smaller so the exposed representative group remains readable.

parts.name: 80-Layer Tick Comb
parts.role: Scale marker indicating that the visible trays are representative of an 80-layer sequence.

parts.name: Layer 80 Final Global Tray
parts.role: Final full-context global layer feeding the tied vocabulary head.

parts.name: Exploded Attention Pre-RMSNorm
parts.role: Representative pre-attention RMSNorm tile shown outside the tray so it is not hidden by the layer block.

parts.name: Exploded GQA QKV Projection
parts.role: Fused projection producing 48 query heads and 8 shared key/value heads.
parts.algorithm:
Q = x @ W_Q
K = x @ W_K
V = x @ W_V
Q, K = qk_rmsnorm(Q, K)

parts.name: Exploded QK-Norm Pair
parts.role: Paired RMSNorm on Q and K, preserved from Gemma 3 as a stability feature.

parts.name: RoPE Base Selector Gear
parts.role: Rotary-position selector: base 10000 for local trays and projected base 4000000 for global trays.

parts.name: Local-or-Global Mask Gate
parts.role: Mask gate selecting either 512-token sliding-window attention or full causal attention.

parts.name: FlashAttention Kernel Bay
parts.role: Attention compute bay using the selected mask and reading KV from local rings or global cache.

parts.name: Attention O Projection
parts.role: Output projection returning attention results to the d=7168 residual stream.

parts.name: Exploded Attention Post-RMSNorm
parts.role: Post-attention RMSNorm tile showing the dual-norm placement explicitly.

parts.name: Exploded FFN Pre-RMSNorm
parts.role: Pre-FFN RMSNorm shown as a separate service tile before the dense SwiGLU block.

parts.name: Dense SwiGLU FFN Bay
parts.role: Dense non-MoE feed-forward bay with d_ff projected near 28672.
parts.memory_footprint: 3 × d × d_ff × BF16 ≈ 1.23 GiB per layer.

parts.name: Exploded FFN Post-RMSNorm
parts.role: Post-FFN RMSNorm tile before the FFN branch rejoins the residual stream.

parts.name: Attention Residual Merge Link
parts.role: Visible link returning the exploded attention branch to the central residual spine.

parts.name: FFN Residual Merge Link
parts.role: Visible link returning the exploded FFN branch to the central residual spine.

parts.name: Global KV Cache Column
parts.role: Tall memory column for full-context KV from global layers, dominating long-context storage.
parts.memory_footprint: 1M × 8 KV heads × 128 head dim × K/V × 10 global layers ≈ 40 GiB FP16 before projected INT4 compression.

parts.name: Local 512-Token KV Ring
parts.role: Compact ring buffer showing that local layers keep only a 512-token window.
parts.memory_footprint: Projected local cache is small because it stores 512 tokens rather than the full 1M context.

parts.name: Latent Summary Cache Bank
parts.role: Projected persistent latent cache for shared long prompts, mounted beside global attention rather than floating above it.
parts.memory_footprint: Projected around 1 KB per cached prompt prefix per layer.
parts.algorithm:
latent = compress(prompt_kv)
out = attn(Q, concat(latent, K), concat(latent, V))

parts.name: Latent Capsule A
parts.role: Visible stored prompt latent connected to the summary cache bank.

parts.name: Latent Capsule B
parts.role: Second stored prompt latent showing that the cache can hold multiple reusable prefixes.

parts.name: Tied LM Head
parts.role: Tied projection from residual width back to the 256K vocabulary logits.

parts.name: CE plus KL Distillation Loss
parts.role: Training loss node combining next-token cross entropy with KL to the Gemini teacher.

parts.name: Frozen Gemini Teacher Slab
parts.role: Frozen larger Gemini model whose logits supervise the projected Gemma student.

parts.name: 25T-Token Multimodal Corpus Tray
parts.role: Projected pretraining data tray for text, image-text, and audio-text examples.

parts.name: AdamW Moment Block m
parts.role: First AdamW moment-state block, one of the two optimizer tensors that double training memory.
parts.memory_footprint: One optimizer state tensor approximately equals parameter size.

parts.name: AdamW Moment Block v
parts.role: Second AdamW moment-state block completing the projected 2× optimizer-memory overhead.
parts.memory_footprint: Second optimizer state tensor approximately equals parameter size.

parts.name: TPU Parallelism Frame
parts.role: Open training frame for tensor parallelism, FSDP, and data parallelism; no expert-parallel lane is present because the model is dense.

parts.name: TPU Mesh Crossbar
parts.role: Communication crossbar showing collectives between tensor, FSDP, and data-parallel shards.
